chapter_title: Concerning the Three Things that were established by the Light
chapter_note: The chapter is overwhelmingly eschatological-cosmological teaching in an impersonal, systematic threefold structure (new earth/coffin/final lump and eternal separation). Aside from a brief hagiographic opening, there is no clear institutional or NT overlay; the “sinners/condemned by deeds” language reads as part of the cosmological mechanics rather than pastoral regulation.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic hagiographic opening (“Once again… disciples… mystery of his knowledge”), functioning as editorial container rather than teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: Three things would be fashioned by the Light through necessity. For there can be no other way nor other result, to allow them to stay without coming about. For the Darkness, the Enemy, must be bound by them; he who stood up against the Light from the beginning. Due to this, these things have no (other) result, to allow them to stay without coming about.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal, systemic exposition: a numbered triad grounded in cosmological necessity, with personified principles (Light/Darkness/Enemy) and no audience-directed application.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, the first thing is the new luminous earth, which was set and built on top of this earth [ ... ] it, namely that alien body [ ... ] built upon it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the numbered triad with cosmic architecture (new earth built over this earth); remains cosmos→cosmos despite lacunae.

paragraphs.core_text: The second thing is this: They will [ ... ] and they [ ... ] the new earth, the coffin [ ... ] of the dark fire, the companion of the Enemy.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second item of the triad; technical eschatological mechanism (coffin/prison imagery) aimed at binding the Enemy, not institutional exhortation. (Page marker removed.)

paragraphs.core_text: The third thing is the souls of all the sinners who have been condemned by their deeds. They were [ ... ] over them woe; they have been condemned according to the wicked deeds they had committed, and due to this they will be crucified on the Enemy, he who had raised himself up against the Greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third item completes the triad and remains within eschatological mechanics (souls affixed to the Enemy). The moral vocabulary (“sinners/condemned”) reads here as part of the cosmic sorting process rather than later church discipline.

paragraphs.core_text: They will seal up this final lump when all the likenesses and images of every shape will be nailed in it. Also, those will be bound by this last fetter for eternity, and be placed as a footstool and a mat and a rag for this coffin [ ... ] which is the prison of the Enemy. It will be placed, being a boundary-marker and a great void between the two, between the Darkness and the Enemy, so that they cannot reach one another, nor can they hear their voices; rather they will become sterile as they are separated from each other for ever and ever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Highly characteristic core cosmological-eschatological description: ‘final lump’, eternal fetter, boundary/void, and sterilizing separation of Darkness from the Enemy—system mechanics without citations or institutional referents.
